newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish civil servants get 4.25 pct rise over 2yrs.
newsitem.headline: Danish civil servants get 4.25 pct rise over 2yrs.

text.p: Denmark's 200,000 state employees on Friday agreed a two-year wage deal giving rises totalling 4.25 percent over the 24-month period, Finance Minister Mogens Lykketoft told a news conference.
"The rises are divided into 1.85 percent during the first year and the remainder in the second year," he said.

He added that of the 4.25 percent, 2.9 would be paid on basic salary while 1.35 percent would go on areas such as increased pensions, educational courses, staff upgrades and support for staff representation.
Lykketoft described the deal, reached after 17 hours of negotiation, as "economically viable".
"There is nothing in the agreement that threatens the good condition in which the Danish economy, as a whole, now stands," he said.
Local authority workers' representatives are to open negotiations on February 26.
Analysts expect them to also agree a two-year pay deal although the amount of their wage increase remains to be seen.
